decisions.reason: The candidate's same-message INTRODUCE already defines logging after each Reel and recording the Instagram Reel link; the publication-format change requires no additional state change.
The candidate's same-message MODIFY already captures the one-per-day cadence and 6 PM to 9 PM window; specifying Reel as the publication format does not alter that schedule.
Publishing approved clips as Instagram Reels does not change the dedicated account's creation, profile configuration, or audience-routing requirements.
The requirement already covers every published clip, so identifying the Instagram publication format as Reel does not change its tracking coverage or metrics.
The candidate's same-message INTRODUCE already records the required caption, hashtags, and account tag placement; publication format does not modify those metadata rules.
The Reel-format decision does not change who approves clips, which clips may be published, or how rejected clips are handled; the same-message approval observation is already represented separately.
Instagram Reels is already one of the candidate's target channels, and publishing this approved batch as Reels does not remove or change the YouTube Shorts and TikTok targets.

Specifying Instagram Reel as the publishing format does not necessarily revise the five-clip production deliverable; the instruction to publish three approved clips does not explicitly cancel or replace the earlier required batch count.
The publication-format change has no effect on whether background music is required, its volume, or its mood-selection rule.
Publishing the approved clips as Instagram Reels does not change the existing 45-to-60-second duration requirement.
The publication format does not change the permitted source videos, topic constraints, selection exclusions, or moment-selection criteria.
Publishing approved clips as Reels does not alter the requirement that each clip contain a complete, standalone teaching moment understandable to an unfamiliar viewer.
